2027-07-09.title: How to Be Certain
2027-07-09.verse: Now many have undertaken to compile an account of the things that have been fulfilled among us, like the accounts passed on to us by those who were eyewitnesses and servants of the word from the beginning. So it seemed good to me as well, because I have followed all things carefully from the beginning, to write an orderly account for you, most excellent Theophilus, so that you may know for certain the things you were taught.
2027-07-09.observation: The Gospel of Luke was written by a physician turned investigative journalist. We can see in the first verses the reason for Luke writing this Gospel. He is writing an orderly account so that the one who commissioned him (Theophilus) can be certain of the truth of everything he has been taught. Little did they know the Holy Spirit was using their efforts and inspired this for us all. Luke realized the way to be certain of faith is to investigate it. Faith that cannot be tested is faith that cannot be trusted. Therefore, he found eyewitnesses, talked to people who were there, and discovered what was true. This is the same for us today. We can follow the truth wherever it leads without fear. The truth always leads us back to the Lord. I heard someone recently say, “Yes, there are a few hard things that Christians have to answer with topics such as the problem of evil. However, while we have to answer a couple of hard questions, atheists have to answer all the rest of them.”
2027-07-09.application: Never be afraid to investigate what you have heard. Always follow the truth.
2027-07-09.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for being trustworthy and revealing Yourself to us in a way that we can trust You.

2027-07-10.title: Where Can We Find You?
2027-07-10.verse: But he replied, “Why were you looking for me? Didn’t you know that I must be in my Father’s house?
2027-07-10.observation: Imagine you moved to a new city. A few months later, some friends are driving through town and they want to surprise you. As hard as it is, they don’t reach out to see where you are. Instead, they have to follow your footsteps and inquire from people you may have met. Would anyone think to go to the local churches to hear if you have been there? Would they expect that you were in your Heavenly Father’s House? We need to make God such a priority in our lives that the House of God would be the first place they would have looked.
2027-07-10.application: Orient your life so that people know by your habits that you are pursuing God.
2027-07-10.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for showing us the way in Your Word.

2027-07-11.title: You Bring God Great Joy
2027-07-11.verse: and the Holy Spirit descended on him in bodily form like a dove. And a voice came from heaven, “You are my one dear Son; in you I take great delight.
2027-07-11.observation: Look at the love the Father shows to the Son. He pours that same love on us. We are dearly loved by God. This is one of the greatest joys that the enemy wants to hide from us. We live lives where we feel we must constantly prove ourselves and all our relationships are conditional. When it comes to God, He already loves us. The Father said this to the Son before He had ever worked a single miracle or preached a single message. God doesn’t love you because of your performance. He loves you because you are His.
2027-07-11.application: Think about the love of God today and focus on how unchanging it is.
2027-07-11.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for loving us completely, wholly, and unreservedly.

2027-07-12.title: The Fortress of Solitude
2027-07-12.verse: The next morning Jesus departed and went to a deserted place. Yet the crowds were seeking him, and they came to him and tried to keep him from leaving them.
2027-07-12.observation: Long before the comic books told us that Superman would go find solitude, Jesus was doing it. Many times, the crowds and distractions of life become too much. They can stop us from being able to focus on what matters most. Jesus needed solitude so He could show up for the mission. If Jesus modeled solitude for us, we should have regular times of being away from the noise of the crowd, too. This might mean putting down our phones, turning off our music, or taking walks without distraction. Whatever that is for you, do it and watch what happens.
2027-07-12.application: Take 10 minutes today and just be still and silent. Could you make the whole 10 without reaching for something?
2027-07-12.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for waiting for us in the stillness.

2027-07-13.title: God Calls Us Deeper
2027-07-13.verse: When he had finished speaking, he said to Simon, “Put out into the deep water and lower your nets for a catch.
2027-07-13.observation: Jesus was telling them to go back out to where they had previously been unsuccessful. However, this time was different. This time, the Lord was with them. Many times, the Lord will have us go back into a world that has not always been kind, helpful, or easy. However, this time is different. This time, the Lord is with us. What would it look like if you went into your world today, but this time you realize the Lord is with you? Would it change how you talked with people? Would it change your level of confidence when encountering difficulty? This doesn’t mean it will always be easy. Problems will come. People will be hard. Issues will arise. However, you can have the confidence that nothing will stop the Lord from walking beside you whispering, “You’re never alone. I am here and will never leave.”
2027-07-13.application: Walk into your world with the confident joy that the Holy Spirit is walking right beside you today.
2027-07-13.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for being our Lord, Savior, King, and Friend.

2027-07-14.title: Right-Side-Up Kingdom
2027-07-14.verse: But I say to you who are listening: Love your enemies, do good to those who hate you, bless those who curse you, pray for those who mistreat you. To the person who strikes you on the cheek, offer the other as well, and from the person who takes away your coat, do not withhold your tunic either. Give to everyone who asks you, and do not ask for your possessions back from the person who takes them away. Treat others in the same way that you would want them to treat you. “If you love those who love you, what credit is that to you? For even sinners love those who love them.
2027-07-14.observation: We can read Scriptures like today’s passage and think, “This sounds upside down from what seems like common sense.” Doesn’t it make sense to do the exact opposite? If someone is your enemy, you should want bad for them. If someone is demanding, you should resist them. We should love those who love us, and hate those who hate us. What Jesus says seems to be upside down. However, this is the way of the Kingdom. It is not Jesus who is upside down, it is us. Jesus came to take this upside down world, and turn it right-side-up again. We are to love people, serve people, and reach out to people because we are not of this world. We are from the Kingdom of God. We have been born again into a Heavenly Kingdom and are now seen as Children of God in the eyes of God. Therefore, we see the world for what it truly is. Our enemy is the devil. Everyone else is in various levels of brokenness. We can now see the way the King sees and it changes how we see everything else.
2027-07-14.application: Think of everyone you meet today as someone with the capacity for good, but locked into an upside down world. This doesn’t mean we trust everyone. It DOES mean we serve with our eyes open.
2027-07-14.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for seeing this possible goodness in all of us. Help us to pray for others to find it as well.

2027-07-16.title: Impressive Faith
2027-07-16.verse: When Jesus heard this, he was amazed at him. He turned and said to the crowd that followed him, “I tell you, not even in Israel have I found such faith!
2027-07-16.observation: In today’s passage, there are many things going on. It was already a big deal that a Roman officer was “asking” anything of a Jew. He wouldn’t have wanted to associate in any way with a Jew that placed him in need. He could have easily tried to demand. However, this Roman officer realized that Jesus was no ordinary man. He was willing to come to Jesus. He didn’t require Jesus to give him special attention. He was so humble about it that he didn’t even come to Jesus himself. He sent a friend. The faith this man had in Jesus was impressive. He knew Jesus could heal without even being there in person. Jesus was amazed. Is Jesus amazed by your faith? Do you make His eyebrows go up and say, “That’s awesome.”?
2027-07-16.application: Can you more fully trust Jesus today?
2027-07-16.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for being completely trustworthy.

2027-07-17.title: The Seed of God’s Word
2027-07-17.verse: Now the parable means this: The seed is the word of God.
2027-07-17.observation: I love how Jesus describes the Word of God in this parable. He calls it the seed. In the parable, it was the seed that had different impacts on the soil it was placed in. However, this is something we tend to frequently overlook. The seed had an impact in every type of soil. One of the greatest pleasures we experience is to hear the powerful Word of God. We also know that we never leave unchanged when we slow down and truly hear what God’s Word says.
2027-07-17.application: Spend time reflecting on God’s Word.
2027-07-17.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for Your powerful, life-changing Word.

2027-07-18.title: A Disciple Is a Follower
2027-07-18.verse: Then he said to them all, “If anyone wants to become my follower, he must deny himself, take up his cross daily, and follow me.
2027-07-18.observation: In the modern world of social media, following someone has changed. Many now think of following as something you do by checking in on someone from time to time or when they post new content. Following in the time of Jesus would have been very different. It might have seemed overwhelming. When you followed someone, you tuned out all other voices and placed them at the center of your life. You took a chance because you ignored all other opportunities. You fully devoted yourself to them. When it comes to Jesus, this is the only way Jesus will accept followers. We cannot halfway follow Him. There is no one more miserable than a “halfway Christian.” However, when we come to fully follow Him, there is true joy.
2027-07-18.application: Is there an area of your life that you have not submitted to fully following Jesus? What course correction do you need to take?
2027-07-18.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for taking all of us and leaving nothing out. You want all of us to experience the freedom You provide.

2027-07-19.title: Pray and Go First
2027-07-19.verse: He said to them, “The harvest is plentiful, but the workers are few. Therefore ask the Lord of the harvest to send out workers into his harvest.
2027-07-19.observation: As a pastor for a long time, I have had the honor of walking with people through various ups and downs. In both situations, people are drawn either toward or away from the Lord. When bad things happen in the world, I have heard so many people say that someone should do something. When something good happens, I have heard the same. People have said someone should get out there and tell people it was the Lord. In both cases, the only issue is they are expecting someone else to do something. God’s Word says the harvest is always ripe. The issue is there is no one willing to roll up their sleeves and do something about it. So, no matter what you are celebrating or mourning, you are not powerless. The harvest is always ripe and ready. The challenge is harvesters. Will you be one? Will you take your pain or take your excitement and use it as a springboard to tell someone about Jesus?
2027-07-19.application: Pray for the Lord to open the door for you to share your hope with someone today.
2027-07-19.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for the opportunity to share Your life-giving hope with someone today.

2027-07-20.title: The Love Of Our Father
2027-07-20.verse: So he said to them, “When you pray, say: “‘Father, may your name be honored; may your kingdom come.
2027-07-20.observation: Have you ever thought about the fact that God has given us the privilege of calling Him Father? He is the Creator of all. He created the term “fatherhood.” He created the symbol of good fatherhood. He could have made it so that we saw Him differently. However, He created the concept of what a good father is so that we would know what He wants to be in our lives. Then, when Jesus (God) teaches us how to talk to Him, Jesus says we should call Him Father. If you have ever talked to someone who never had a father, this becomes even more profound. One of the most powerful moments is the first time a father-figure says, “You can call me dad if you want.”  Our God and King has looked at us and said, “You can call me Father.”
2027-07-20.application: Have you ever thought about how God created the relationship of Father and child so we could know how to relate to Him? Does that change how you see Him?
2027-07-20.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for teaching us to call God our Father and for loving us the way You do.

2027-07-21.title: The Joy of the Father
2027-07-21.verse: Do not be afraid, little flock, for your Father is well pleased to give you the kingdom.
2027-07-21.observation: It is easy to forget that we are all here because God wanted us to be, and we are invited into the Kingdom of God because He is excited to bring us into His “home.” I heard someone once try to describe the joy of God in creating us. He said, “We were created from the laughter of the Trinity.” This is not true in a literal sense, but the idea is solid. God created joy. He exists as a Triune Godhead: Father, Son, and Spirit. It is in this perfect relationship that He called us into being. He has joy in inviting us to re-enter the original state we were created for. Back in the Garden of Eden, humans existed in the perfect Earth God had made, and He fellowshipped with us. He has joy in inviting us back to that.
2027-07-21.application: Think about the joy God has in having you in His Kingdom. You are loved more than you can imagine.
2027-07-21.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for loving us.

2027-07-22.title: God Alone Measures True Worth
2027-07-22.verse: But indeed, some are last who will be first, and some are first who will be last.
2027-07-22.observation: Many people spend most of their life in a desperate comparison game. They are constantly looking at those to their left and right to measure their value and worth. Are they keeping up? Are they in front or behind? Do people see their value and are they being given what their perceived worth demands? It is exhausting and difficult to ever feel at peace. Jesus teaches that appearances are often deceiving. Those who seem important now will be the least in the Kingdom of Heaven. Also, those who you will never notice in this life will be giants in the world to come. I have a feeling that when we get to Heaven, we will be amazed at what God counted and what He didn’t care about. Therefore, the goal is to always be looking to the Lord. Allow Him to be our measure of worth. Trust that He sees us, knows us, and we do the best we can because of His love.
2027-07-22.application: Do the best you can, today, not to gain the approval of others but because you already have your Heavenly Father’s approval.
2027-07-22.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for sending the Holy Spirit to walk with us and help us each step of the way.

2027-07-23.title: Count the Cost
2027-07-23.verse: If anyone comes to me and does not hate his own father and mother, and wife and children, and brothers and sisters, and even his own life, he cannot be my disciple. Whoever does not carry his own cross and follow me cannot be my disciple. For which of you, wanting to build a tower, doesn’t sit down first and compute the cost to see if he has enough money to complete it?
2027-07-23.observation: Jesus tells us to consider the path before walking the path. Think hard about what we are doing when we desire salvation. This is not because He does not want us to be saved. He knows that the commitment to follow Him will require all of us. You cannot halfway follow God and be successful. It requires all of us. That would be like someone who desires to go back to school to better their education. A good academic advisor would stop them first and suggest they count the cost. It will take extra hours of study. It will be a financial commitment. It will mean saying no to fun outings so you can attend class. But, once you have made up your mind, go for it. This is the same with Jesus. Make up your mind. Let’s take this adventure together.
2027-07-23.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for being honest with us about what it will cost to follow You.

2027-07-24.title: The Joy of the Lord
2027-07-24.verse: It was appropriate to celebrate and be glad, for your brother was dead, and is alive; he was lost and is found.’
2027-07-24.observation: There are so many moments worth examining in the parable of the prodigal son. That’s the beauty of a parable. A parable is a complex spiritual principle wrapped in a story. This means that there are many different things we can take away from the principle because it is explained with “flesh on it.” The moment in this passage that I love is when the Father comes running to the lost son. Then, at the end of the story, He shares why. He sees His son coming home as a rebirth. I know many people who have lost loved ones and they would all admit they would give almost anything to see them one more time. This is what the Father experiences and He is overjoyed. It is important to remember who is telling this story. Jesus, the second member of the Trinity, is telling us what happens to God when one of His lost children comes back again. He is saying, “No one knows the Father as well as the Spirit and Me. I’m telling you, when you come back to Him, He is overjoyed in a way I cannot fully express in words.” That’s how much the Lord loves you.
2027-07-24.application: Take a moment and think about seeing a lost loved one again. Then imagine that is how God felt when you “came home” to Him.
2027-07-24.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for showing us the love of the Father and for loving us the way You do.

2027-07-25.title: Did You Do The Dishes?
2027-07-25.verse: The one who is faithful in a very little is also faithful in much, and the one who is dishonest in a very little is also dishonest in much. If then you haven’t been trustworthy in handling worldly wealth, who will entrust you with the true riches? And if you haven’t been trustworthy with someone else’s property, who will give you your own?
2027-07-25.observation: In this passage, Jesus is teaching a powerful principle about doing the little things well if you want to be trusted with more. When my girls were little, I worked to teach this principle. The house rules were that if you completed your chores, you would be allowed to do all the other fun things that came along. Therefore, when one of my children would ask if they could go to a friend’s house, I would ask, “Did you do the dishes?” This was my wife’s and my way of saying that you dictate whether or not you get to go. So, do you get to go? Jesus is saying the same. We dictate what blessings He allows into our life based on how we handle what He has already given us. Why would God give us a family if we do not take care of ourselves? Why would God give us a new job if we are not doing our best where we are? However, the opposite is true. If we are being faithful and doing our best, God sees and will reward in due time.
2027-07-25.application: Are you giving your best effort?
2027-07-25.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for all the opportunities around us that are sometimes disguised as hard work.

2027-07-26.title: Persistence Pays Off
2027-07-26.verse: And those who were in front scolded him to get him to be quiet, but he shouted even more, “Son of David, have mercy on me!
2027-07-26.observation: In today’s passage, the blind man would not stop yelling for Jesus. He didn’t care who heard him nor what they thought of him. He was not going to quit until he got to Jesus. I have heard many people say that we need to know when to let go and when to quit. This is true. The Bible says there is a time for all things. However, we need to take a moment to realize and remember there is a time to keep pushing and be persistent. Just because something is hard does not mean it is not meant to be tried. Sometimes, the harder it is, the sweeter the victory. What if today was not the day you decided to quit? What if you waited until tomorrow? What if you tried to move forward one more day? How do you know? Does it honor God? Does it promote spiritual growth? Does it move you closer to Him and further away from self-harm? If so, push one more day.
2027-07-26.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for walking with us through every hard day of faithful persistence.

2027-07-27.title: Go All In
2027-07-27.verse: When Jesus heard this, he said to him, “One thing you still lack. Sell all that you have and give the money to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. Then come, follow me.
2027-07-27.observation: In poker, there is a phrase called going “all in.” This is when you want to win the round so badly that you will bet all of your money. You don’t leave any reserves. This means you push all your chips to the middle of the table. Everything is riding on your ability to win with the cards you have been dealt. This is what Jesus was challenging this young man to do. We do not see Jesus challenging anyone else to sell all they have. Jesus realized this was the last “chip” he was holding back. If we are to follow Jesus, we must go “all in” with Him and surrender our lives. Only then do we find that we have an eternally winning hand. There is no need to fear going “all in” with Jesus. He has already conquered the world.
2027-07-27.application: Go “all in” with Jesus. Is there anything you are holding back?
2027-07-27.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for being worthy of it all.

2027-07-28.title: What is God Looking For?
2027-07-28.verse: And the king said to him, ‘Well done, good slave! Because you have been faithful in a very small matter, you will have authority over ten cities.’
2027-07-28.observation: Have you ever watched someone make a splash in the world and wondered if God expects the same for you? Maybe you see other people succeed in life and feel as though you are a failure because you do not see the same success happening in the same way. What does God expect of us? What does it mean to be successful in the kingdom of God? In this parable, notice what Jesus praised about the servant. Jesus showed that his faithfulness is what was rewarded. He was faithful with what he had. That’s it. God did not expect the person given less to produce as much as the one given more. He was expecting each one to be faithful and do the best they could with what they had been given. So ask yourself, are you doing the best you can with what you have been given? Be totally honest. If the answer is yes, then you are doing exactly what God is looking for. Praise the Lord. However, if you can honestly say you are not giving your best and doing all you can with the gifts, talents, abilities, and opportunities you have been given… it’s time to course correct.
2027-07-28.application: Be faithful. Give God everything and realize that success is up to Him.
2027-07-28.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for giving us all we need to do all You have called us to do.

2027-07-29.title: Dual Citizens
2027-07-29.verse: So he said to them, “Then give to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s, and to God the things that are God’s.
2027-07-29.observation: Jesus talked about the Kingdom of God to the point His enemies thought they could ruin Him by speaking about the “kingdoms of men.” His focus was on helping people understand we are part of a dual citizenship. Our primary allegiance is to the Heavenly Kingdom. This automatically makes us good citizens of the other kingdom. However, we must never forget there is a divide. We honor the kingdoms of men, but our primary allegiance is to the kingdom of God. Jesus said this when He said we should give to the world what belongs to the world, and give to God what belongs to God. This is the right answer on how we operate in our lives today. The line is when the two kingdoms disagree. That’s when we honor God over any other allegiance. We see this in the book of Acts. In Acts 5, the apostles are told to stop speaking about Jesus. They said they had to obey God because they were witnesses of something wonderful.
2027-07-29.application: Do you sometimes struggle with being a dual citizen? Is there an area where you need to honor God more than men?
2027-07-29.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for teaching us how to be IN the world, but not OF the world.

2027-07-31.title: It’s the Heart, Not the Amount
2027-07-31.verse: He said, “I tell you the truth, this poor widow has put in more than all of them. For they all offered their gifts out of their wealth. But she, out of her poverty, put in everything she had to live on.
2027-07-31.observation: The Lord takes a moment to watch people giving into the Temple treasury. I love that the Lord has said it wasn’t the amount that mattered to Him. It was the heart behind it. This is important because many feel they do not have the same skills, opportunities, or finances as others do. The Lord is making it clear. That does not matter to Him. What matters is what you do with what you have been given. So, stop comparing yourself to others. Compare yourself to who you would be without Jesus.
2027-07-31.application: Do the best you can with what you have and leave the results to Jesus in the light of eternity.
2027-07-31.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for giving us all the opportunity to make a difference at a level we can handle.
